 Red Sox Acquire Nick Fortes
 By Darragh McDonald |
 at November 18, 2026 2:05pm CDT 
 The Red Sox have acquired catcher Nick Fortes from the Rays, according to announcements from both clubs. Tampa gets minor league right-hander Angel Roa in return. The Sox designated catcher Connor Wong to open a 40-man spot for Fortes. Jeff Passan of ESPN first reported that the Sox were acquiring Fortes. Chris Cotillo of MassLive first reported Roa’s inclusion and Wong’s DFA .
 It’s probably not a coincidence that this deal came together just before Friday’s non-tender deadline. The Red Sox and Rays both have a starter behind the plate, as Boston has Adley Rutschman and Tampa has Liam Hicks . Each club also went into the winter with an arbitration-eligible backup on the roster, the Rays with Fortes and the Red Sox with Wong.
 MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz projects Wong for a $2MM salary next year. Fortes is projected slightly higher at $3.4MM. Wong’s defense doesn’t get strong grades. He seemed like maybe he was breaking out at the plate in 2024 when he hit 13 home runs and slashed .280/.333/.425. Unfortunately, he has hit .214/.287/.299 over the past two seasons. That has made him replacement level or worse for that span.
 Wong still has an option remaining. The Sox could have tendered him a contract and kept him as depth in the minors, but they also have Mickey Gasper on the roster. Gasper is also still optionable and he is cheaper because he hasn’t qualified for arbitration yet. The Sox have decided to move on from Wong. They have some time to work out a trade but the most likely outcome is that he will be non-tendered on Friday.
 Fortes should be a better backup than Wong. Fortes generally gets decent grades for his work with the pads on. His 2026 numbers were a bit worse than league average but he still has positive numbers for his total body of work.
 Offensively, he’s not a huge threat but he’s fine. Over the past two years, he has made 565 trips to the plate. His 4.6% walk rate in that time is way below average but he also struck out at a 16.3% clip that is better than par. He hit 11 home runs and slashed .246/.301/.364. That leads to an 86 wRC+, indicating he has been 14% below the league average hitter. Catchers are usually 10 to 12% below par on the whole, so that’s an acceptable range for a backup with a decent defensive reputation.
